instruction: nx.k_components(G) (networkx/algorithms/connectivity/kcomponents.py, the exact Moody and White algorithm) loses or truncates k-components on some graphs. A k-component is a maximal set of nodes whose induced subgraph has node connectivity at least k; the result maps each k to the list of k-components. Two failures to fix: (1) take two icosahedra, nodes 0-11 (nx.icosahedral_graph()) and 12-23 (the same graph relabelled i -> i + 12), and add connector node 24 joined to 0, 1, 2, 12, 13; node 25 joined to 3, 4, 5, 14, 15; node 26 joined to 6, 7, 8, 16, 17; and node 27 joined to 9, 10, 20, 21. The graph is 4-connected, so for k = 1 to 4 the only k-component is all 28 nodes, and its 5-components are the two icosahedra, but one of them is missing from the result. (2) G = nx.gnp_random_graph(16, 0.6, seed=22070) is 7-connected, so for every k from 1 to 7 the only k-component is the whole graph, yet some levels report smaller fragments instead. Results on other graphs must stay correct. Add tests.
